subject: Orchestra launch: thresholds and traffic projection
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-01T09:15:00-08:00
Subject: Orchestra launch: thresholds and traffic projection

Karthik —

Quick intro: Orchestra is planning a staged public launch for their new orchestration UI the week of Jan 10. They asked for a temporary uplift in rate limits for two weeks around the initial ramp to ensure no customer-visible throttles during the first 72h after GA.

As a baseline I need the following from infra/product:
- A recommended rate threshold (calls/s) and token throughput for their primary endpoint (/v1/generate) to support 30k DAU with a 95th percentile latency target of 300ms.
- Any gating product asks (model variant, cached vs uncached path, sequence length assumptions) so we can finalize the entitlement.
- A short rollback/fallback plan if we hit capacity limits.

They've shared an internal projection (attached) — it's conservative but shows a sharp ramp on day 1 then a 48h plateau. Can we get an initial read by EOD Friday so I can set expectations with the customer?

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

Attachment: Orchestra_weekly_traffic_v1.xlsx (xlsx)
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-02T11:30:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Orchestra launch: thresholds and traffic projection

Marissa — thanks for the heads up and the attachment. A couple quick clarifying questions before we commit numbers:

1) Endpoint mix: is /v1/generate the only heavy endpoint, or will they hit embeddings/rerank endpoints during onboarding? If there is reranking we need separate capacity slices.
2) Sequence length distribution: rough P50/P95 tokens per request — are these 64/512, 128/1k, etc.? Cost and latency change significantly with longer sequences.
3) Can we get the 72-hour hourly breakdown (not just daily)? We optimize for burst windows, and hourly spikes matter for our continuous batching logic.

From a product perspective:
- If they can accept the smaller quantized variant (q4) for non-SLA-critical paths we can drop unit cost and increase headroom.
- We should decide on a prefix/KV caching policy for repeated chat histories; that affects steady-state token counts.

David/Priyom — can the infra team provision a temporary entitlement patch and a short-lived reserve pool we can toggle? If so, what's the minimum notice and lead time?

I'll carve a strawman number after we get the hourly breakdown.

— Karthik
Head of Serving Reliability, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Sara Nunez <sara@orchestralabs.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-08T10:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Orchestra launch: thresholds and traffic projection

Karthik / team — attaching an hourly slice for the first 5 days and a summary of typical request shapes. Sara: included you here so infra/product have the direct shape we expect.

Highlights from the attachment (Orchestra_weekly_traffic_v1.xlsx):
- Day 1: spike to ~22k calls/min for a 3-hour window during US morning, then settles to ~6k calls/min.
- Expected P50 seq length: 80 tokens; P95: 420 tokens.
- ~15% of requests are batch-like (bulk ingestion) hitting embeddings endpoints; the rest are interactive generate calls.

Customer asks:
- A temporary 3x rate bump for /v1/generate for 72h after GA, then step down to a 1.5x uplift for 10 days while they ramp.
- Clear rollback contract: if we detect sustained >85% utilisation on any pod for >30 min, Redwood will automatically route new traffic to a cold fallback model and throttle non-critical batch jobs.

Let me know if the above is actionable and what minimal entitlements look like.

Thanks —
Marissa

Attachment: Orchestra_weekly_traffic_v1.xlsx (updated): hourly slices and endpoint mix
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Sara Nunez <sara@orchestralabs.com>
Date: 2026-12-20T15:40:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Orchestra launch: thresholds and traffic projection

Thanks for the shape, Marissa — that hourly view helps a lot. Strawman entitlement & product asks below (subject to infra confirmation):

Strawman entitlement (Tiered):
- Day 0 (first 72h): /v1/generate = 3x baseline -> target burst capacity ~40k calls/min over 3-hour peak; token throughput provisioning to cover P95 seq lengths (420 tokens) at 95th percentile concurrency.
- Warm period (days 4-14): 1.5x baseline sustained; keep embeddings pool isolated with dedicated q4 quantized instances for cost control.

Product asks / constraints:
- Prefer they use the q4 variant for embeddings and batch ingestion to avoid costing out the dedicated GA path.
- Enable KV prefix caching for interactive flows where conversation ids are stable — this will reduce active token counts by ~20% on our estimations. We need their engineering team to tag stable conversation ids.
- Enforce a max seq length of 1,024 per request in the entitlement to limit runaway requests.

Operational fallback plan (automated):
- If sustained pod CPU/GPU occupancy >85% for 30m -> switch new requests to a compatible, lower-cost fallback model (compatible variant) and reject non-critical batch ingestion with clear 429 messaging including a Retry-After header.
- We will also open a temporary reserve pool (cold instances pre-warmed) that can be toggled within ~45 minutes of an ops request; Priyom/David please confirm lead time.

Next steps:
1) Priyom/David to confirm reserve pool lead time and any ACL/entitlement UI changes needed (ETA?).
2) Legal/Accounts to confirm we can formalize the temporary uplift in the SAAS addendum (Marissa, can you loop them?).
3) Marissa to share final GA date so infra can schedule the toggle windows.

I've attached a lightweight runbook outline (orchestra_entitlement_runbook.md) with the rollback commands and observability checks. Please review and call out edits.

— Karthik
Head of Serving Reliability
Attachment: orchestra_entitlement_runbook.md (md)
From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Sara Nunez <sara@orchestralabs.com>, Orchestra Infra <infra@orchestralabs.com>
Date: 2026-12-28T09:00:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Orchestra launch: thresholds and traffic projection — provisioning confirmation

All — confirming infra can provision the temporary entitlement described below with the following caveats and timings:

- Reserve pool: we will provision a cold reserve pool equivalent to ~35% of the requested Day 0 burst. Cold pool warm-up time is ~45 minutes; full ramp (to accept traffic at targeted latency) generally takes ~90 minutes.
- Toggle lead time: please give us a 2-hour notice window for toggles during weekday business hours; explicit emergency toggles can be executed with 30-minute notice once an on-call engineer is paged.
- Automated rollback: we've implemented the 85% occupancy -> fallback routing rule in staging; will push to prod during a scheduled maintenance window on Jan 8.

Operational attachments: temp_quota_patch.sh (bootstrap script for entitlement flip) — ranbook includes the exact CLI and the observability dashboards to watch (errors, latency, CPU/GPU occupancy, token/sec).

Marissa — please confirm the final GA date and that Orchestra will tag conversation ids for KV caching. Sara, if you can confirm tagging by Jan 5 we can finalize the plan.

I'll coordinate a 30-minute runbook walkthrough with on-call infra the week before GA.

Thanks —
David Kim
Director, Platform Engineering, Redwood Inference
